exact_source_excerpt: The product equals $1+\sqrt{1+d}+\sqrt{1-d}+\sqrt{1-d^2}\le4$, because $\sqrt{1+d}+\sqrt{1-d}\le2$ by concavity of the square root. If $d>1$, then $\abs{x-d}=d-x\ge1-x=\abs{x-1}$ for $x\in[-1,1]$, so $\mathcal J(d)\le\mathcal J(1)=\pi+2\log(1+\sqrt2)<\pi+4\log2$. For \eqref{eq:rearrange}, write $g(y)=\int_0^\infty\1\{g(y)>\sigma\}\dd\sigma$ and $h(y)=\int_0^\infty\1\{h(y)>\tau\}\dd\tau$. For $\sigma,\tau\ge0$ the sets $\{g>\sigma\}$ and $\{h>\tau\}$ are intervals centred at $0$, possibly empty or all of $\R$, and $\{y:h(y-b)>\tau\}$ is the translate of the second by $b$. The length of the intersection of two intervals is at most the length of the shorter one, with equality when they have the same centre. Hence $\abs{\{g>\sigma\}\cap(b+\{h>\tau\})}\le\abs{\{g>\sigma\}\cap\{h>\tau\}}$, and integrating over $\sigma$ and $\tau$ with Tonelli's theorem gives \eqref{eq:rearrange}.

exact_source_excerpt: (a) The $(i,j)$ entry of $DAD$ is $\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_ja_{ij}$, which equals $a_{ij}$ when $i$ and $j$ lie in the same part and $-a_{ij}$ otherwise. (b) Order the coordinates so that $I$ comes first; then $C=\begin{pmatrix}0&M\\M^T&0\end{pmatrix}$ with $M=A_{I,J}$. Let $M=\sum_k\sigma_ku_kv_k^T$ be a singular value decomposition, with $\sigma_k>0$ and orthonormal families $(u_k)$ and $(v_k)$. The vectors $(u_k,\pm v_k)/\sqrt2$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $C$ with eigenvalues $\pm\sigma_k$. Their orthogonal complement consists of the vectors $(x,y)$ with $x$ orthogonal to the range of $M$ and $y$ orthogonal to the range of $M^T$, that is, with $M^Tx=0$ and $My=0$, and on it $C(x,y)=(My,M^Tx)=0$. Hence the singular values of $C$ are the $\sigma_k$, each counted twice, followed by zeros.
